response.sql: WITH album_rates AS (SELECT AlbumId, 1.0 * SUM(Bytes) / SUM(Milliseconds) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track GROUP BY AlbumId), m AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS mean_rate FROM album_rates) SELECT AVG(a.rate) AS avg_rate, AVG(a.track_count) AS avg_track_count, AVG(a.rate - m.mean_rate) AS avg_excess FROM album_rates a CROSS JOIN m WHERE a.rate > m.mean_rate

assumptions.assumption: Albums are formed by grouping Track rows on AlbumId, so only albums with at least one track appear. Tracks with a NULL AlbumId form one group.
The track count is COUNT(*), which includes tracks whose Bytes is NULL. Only the byte sum ignores missing sizes.
Milliseconds is NOT NULL, so only Bytes can be missing. An album whose tracks all have NULL Bytes has a NULL rate. It is left out of the mean and of the above-mean set.
The mean is the unweighted average of the album rates, not total bytes divided by total milliseconds.
